messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - multiple egress failures observed from AZ-B affecting NAT translations for several customer VPCs (alert: egress-error-rate > 15% over 2m). Paging @sara (oncall). Link: https://monitoring.redwood.test/alerts/3921234567

sara (oncall): grabbing. oncall-in for AZ-B right now?

jake (infra): I can join, seeing increased 5xxs and TCP resets out of azb-nat-1. Cloud WAN shows route flaps around 3921234520.

maria (netops): confirmed. Route table associations in AZ-B show a drift: some subnets briefly pointing to a stale route table (rtb-ghost-azb) that references a decommissioned NAT instance ID.

sam (sre): rolling telemetry: p50 p95 tail latency for hosted-api in eu-west is up 3-4x. Correlates with egress failures.

kate (support): we already have a support ticket from customer: acme-inc — intermittent outbound failures. Customer impact visible on support portal.

sara (oncall): ok, immediate goals: 1) stop customer impact (mitigate), 2) find cause (config drift vs infra). Jake/Maria you two coordinate. Sam watch SLOs and error budget. Kate triage customers & update comms.

jake (infra): mitigation plan: detach the stale association and re-associate correct route table (rtb-azb-prod) to affected subnets. If re-assoc fails, fallback -> provision temporary NAT instance and update route to 0.0.0.0/0 -> eni-temp-nat. Preparing terraform rollback PR to revert recent route-table change.

maria (netops): note: there was a recent infra job that backfilled route-table tags in AZ-B about ~10m ago. I suspect a tagging edge caused the automation to re-apply the wrong table for a small set of subnets. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T08:34:12Z route-assoc job: apply -> subnet-azb-12 -> rtb-ghost-azb
2026-03-15T08:34:15Z route-assoc job: success
```

sam (sre): I'm running a quick canary to validate re-assoc won't spike connections. If we re-assoc, we might break existing conntracking — will need conntrack drain plan.

sara (oncall): do the re-assoc during a controlled window. Kate start external comms template: short message + ETA. Customers count impacted ~12 (internal list).

kate (support): working on message: "We're investigating outbound connectivity issues in AZ-B affecting some services; engineers are performing a mitigation. We'll update within 30 minutes." Adding affected customers.

jake (infra): executing manual re-assoc on one non-critical subnet first: running command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rta-0abc1234 --route-table-id rtb-azb-prod
```

incident-bot: deploy-bot triggered: terraform plan for rollback PR #3789 created by infra-automation at 3921234680.

maria (netops): after manual re-assoc on subnet-azb-12, outbound flows restored for that subnet. conntrack entries were minimal, no mass connection resets.

sam (sre): metrics: error-rate dropped from 18% -> 3% for canary subnet within 45s. p95 latency returning to baseline.

sara (oncall): good. escalate to full remediation: execute bulk re-assoc. Jake coordinate with Maria, Sam to monitor. Kate update customers: mitigation in progress, partial restoration observed, ETA 25m for full remediation.

jake (infra): running bulk script now (native CLI with rate-limit): 
```
for id in $(cat affected_assoc_ids.txt); do aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id $id --route-table-id rtb-azb-prod; sleep 2; done
```

maria (netops): while running, noticing a subset of associations fail with HTTP 409 conflict: association state mismatch. Suspect the automation that applied rtb-ghost-azb is still active and racing.

sara (oncall): -> action: Maria pause route-assoc job in infra-automation. Jake continue manual re-assoc after job paused. Who can pause?

jake (infra): I have access, pausing job via k8s: 
```
kubectl scale deploy route-assoc-job -n infra-automation --replicas=0
```
Paused.

incident-bot: automation-job route-assoc-job scaled to 0 replicas by jake (infra) at 3921234882.

maria (netops): after pause, remaining associations applying cleanly. Bulk complete at 3921234930. Verified: all affected subnets now point to rtb-azb-prod.

sam (sre): SLOs: error-rate back to 1.2%, latency baseline. No elevated retries. Observability shows NAT gateway healthy.

kate (support): updated external message: "Outbound connectivity restored for most customers in AZ-B. We're continuing verification; full resolution ETA 10m. If you still see issues please reply to this thread." :white_check_mark:

sara (oncall): good triage. Root cause hypothesis: automation backfill applied wrong route table (tag collision) + timing caused transient race with live re-assocs -> resulted in egress failures and some conntrack resets. Need postmortem.

jake (infra): created rollback PR #3790 to remove the backfill job and add a safety check (tag-to-rtb mapping pre-validate). Link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/3790

maria (netops): next steps for post-incident: 1) add preflight validation to route-assoc job, 2) add feature flag and dry-run for backfills, 3) run canary across single AZ before bulk.

sam (sre): action items for SRE: run long-tail connection validation, add alerts for route-assoc job churn and detection of stale rtb references, run chaos test in staging for automation race.

kate (support): compiling impacted customer list + timeline for comms. Will prepare draft for status page and support portal.

sara (oncall): handing off to next oncall: @sam will lead postmortem and remediation follow-ups. I will tag the incident as "mitigated" and close the page once postmortem ticket is created. Thanks everyone for quick response. :pray:

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> MITIGATED by sara (oncall) at 3921235250. Follow-up: create incident ticket in JIRA INC-2026 and assign to sam (sre), maria (netops), jake (infra).

sam (sre): created INC-2026 with initial timeline, assigned owners. Will schedule retrospective tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

sara (oncall): handing off fully. Last update: customers mostly restored, automation paused, rollback PR open. If anything regresses ping @oncall immediately.

kate (support): posting support note and closing affected tickets as "monitoring". Will reopen if customer reports repeat issues.

incidents-end: thread closed at 3921235300.
